The '''''Bay of Plenty Times''''' is the regional daily paper for the [[Bay of Plenty]] area, including [[Tauranga]], in the [[North Island]] of [[New Zealand]].

==History==
The ''Bay of Plenty Times'' was first produced on 4 September 1872 as a bi-weekly publication. It consisted of four tabloid-sized pages and cost three pence per issue. The founder and editor was WB Langbridge. Ownership of the newspaper changed many times over the next 40 years, including several times through mortgagee sales. Despite these hardships the ''Times'' issued a Christmas supplement in 1897 which featured one of the earliest use of photographs in New Zealand newspapers.{{Citation needed|date=February 2017}} From 1913 the paper's viability stabilised under the Gifford and Cross families. Both families were associated with the paper until it was sold to Wilson and Horton in 1992. Ownership changed again in 1996 when Independent Newspapers PC from Dublin acquired a controlling interest in Wilson and Horton. In 1976 a fire destroyed the newspaper's entire collection of back issues. The publisher had kept copies on microfilm, which are held by the [[National Library of New Zealand|Alexander Turnbull Library]]. The ''Times'' became more successful from the early 1950s, with its progress linked with the Bay of Plenty's rapid growth since [[Mount Maunganui|Mt Maunganui]] became an export port.<ref>[http://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/cgi-bin/paperspast?a=d&cl=CL1.BOPT&essay=1&e=-------10--1----0-- Bay of Plenty Times archive] natlib.govt.nz</ref> However, from the early 2000s it began to face challenges of declining circulation and advertising. On 5 February 2011, the Saturday edition was re-branded as the ''Bay Of Plenty Times Weekend''. On 4 March 2013, the weekday ''Bay Of Plenty Times'' changed from broadsheet to tabloid format and from afternoon to morning delivery.

The ''Bay of Plenty Times'' has the ninth-largest circulation of New Zealand's 19 daily newspapers, at just under 11,000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://newspaper.abc.org.nz/audit.html?org=npa&publicationid=%25&mode=embargo&npa_admin=1&publicationtype=19&memberid=%25&type=%25|title=Press Audit Results|website=New Zealand Audit Bureau of Circulations|access-date=21 Feb 2019|archive-date=18 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318222653/http://newspaper.abc.org.nz/audit.html?org=npa&publicationid=%25&mode=embargo&npa_admin=1&publicationtype=19&memberid=%25&type=%25|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Other publications==
The ''Bay of Plenty Times'' also publishes the following newspapers:

===''Coastal News''===
The ''Coastal News'' is delivered free every Thursday to [[Whangamatā]], Whiritoa, Onemana, Pauanui, Tairua and up the eastern seaboard to [[Whitianga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Coastal_News.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015060917/http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Coastal_News.pdf |archive-date=2008-10-15 }}</ref>

===''Waihi Leader''===
The ''Waihi Leader'' is distributed free every Thursday to homes in [[Waihi]], Waihi Beach, Athenree, [[Katikati]], Waikino, MacKay Town, Karangahake, [[Paeroa]] and the surrounding areas.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Waihi%20Leader.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015060954/http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Waihi%20Leader.pdf |archive-date=2008-10-15 }}</ref>

===''Katikati Advertiser''===
The ''Katikati Advertiser'' is distributed free every Thursday to all [[Katikati]] urban and rural areas and [[Ōmokoroa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Katikati_Advertiser.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015060935/http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Katikati_Advertiser.pdf |archive-date=2008-10-15 }}</ref>

===''Bay News''===
The ''Bay News'' was distributed every Thursday to homes in [[Papamoa]], [[Te Puke]], [[Mount Maunganui]], [[Welcome Bay]], [[Tauranga]], Bethlehem, Pyes Pa, Te Puna, Katikati, Ōmokoroa, Waihi Beach, [[Waihi]] and [[Whangamatā]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Bay%20News.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015060823/http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Bay%20News.pdf |archive-date=2008-10-15 }}</ref> Publication ceased in 2018.

===''Te Puke Times''===
The ''Te Puke Times'' is distributed free every Thursday to [[Te Puke]], [[Paengaroa]], [[Maketu]], Pukehina, [[Pongakawa]], and [[Welcome Bay]] urban and rural deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Te%20Puke%20Times.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015060900/http://soldonapn.co.nz/resources/regionals/boptimes/community/Te%20Puke%20Times.pdf |archive-date=2008-10-15 }}</ref>
